question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (980f84c); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (bb35517).

answer:
Criterion 2 went through three registered revisions.

1. **Revision 1** (commit b0b2bce, 2026-08-22) defined it as selectivity (real minus control) at the best layer, with a threshold of ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].
2. **Revision 2** (commit 7e6e36a, same day) kept the same statement but marked the threshold "provisional" [crit-rev2-2]. The rows don't say why.
3. **Revision 3** (commit 43b2896, 2026-09-26) is the final form. It replaced the selectivity floor with a leak bound: "Control task shows no leak." The control's maximum balanced accuracy over layers must not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2].

The note on revision 3 gives the reasoning. Under a type-disjoint split, the control task's ceiling is chance, so a selectivity floor doesn't fit. An intermediate draft used 0.50 ± 0.03 (980f84c). It was replaced before the push because a ±0.03 band fires 59–80% of the time even when there is no leak (bb35517). So the permutation-based percentile threshold replaced a fixed tolerance that would have produced frequent false alarms [crit-rev3-2].

This revision cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [crit-rev3-2].
